pool.text: The points A = (2, k), B = (8, 4) and C = (5, 7) form a right-angled triangle with the right angle at B. Find the value of k.
pool.sol:
For a right-angled triangle with the right angle at B, the gradient of AB must be the negative reciprocal of the gradient of BC.

The gradient of AB, \(m_{AB} = \frac{4 - k}{8 - 2} = \frac{4 - k}{6}\).

The gradient of BC, \(m_{BC} = \frac{7 - 4}{5 - 8} = \frac{3}{-3} = -1\).

Since the angle at B is a right angle, \(m_{AB} \times m_{BC} = -1\).

So, \(\frac{4 - k}{6} \times (-1) = -1\).

\(\frac{4 - k}{6} = 1\).

\(4 - k = 6\).

\(k = 4 - 6\).

\(k = -2\). [M1][A1]
